prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: new model sheet for the Huitoto / Murui-Muina visual bible, an original editorial adaptation of credited published Amazonian narratives.
PRIMARY ART DIRECTION: unmistakable, expressive PHYSICAL CUT PAPER, stronger relief and visible construction than a softly textured illustration. Everything is built out of individually cut, folded, curled, interleaved dyed matte PAPER pieces. At first glance the viewer must immediately recognize scissors-cut paper and the real shadows of separated pieces. Show 8 to 12 major overlapping spatial layers, deep stepped silhouettes, genuine empty air between layers, sharply legible inner edges with narrow lighter paper thickness, broad short directional cast shadows, occlusion and contact shadows. Larger foliage sheets fold along their midrib and curl off the plane; fine fibres are actual narrow cut-paper strips. Paper thickness and depth are exaggerated enough to remain readable in a thumbnail, without making every surface busy. Solid colour sheets with restrained visible fibre and small hand-cut irregularities, not a photographic texture filter. Approximately 0.5 to 1 mm paper edges, 3 to 12 mm apparent separation between world planes, varied depending on subject; these are art-making instructions, not measurements of the depicted cultural objects.
Lighting: a consistent warm broad directional light from the upper left, fairly strong diagonal shadows toward the lower right, soft enough to feel editorial, never black theatrical gloom. Clear foreground / middle / distance separation with atmosphere made from physical pale paper layers, not fog effects. A continuous quiet deep forest world fills all image edges. No visible perimeter of a diorama, backing board, base, platform, table, studio, white surround, vignette, picture frame or cutout hole encircling the entire image. The scene extends beyond all four boundaries. Supporting views sit in continuous contextual space without dividing lines or bordered panels. Complete bodies and main objects are fully in frame with breathing room.
Palette continuity: forest green #385745, young green #8C9B58, burnt terracotta #B95737, blue-grey river #304852, cream fibre #CBB389, earth #806348, charcoal #343733, warm pale paper #F3EBDD. Colours are editorial choices, not a community symbolic code. Allow richer light/dark contrast to expose cut-paper layering.
Human faces, when requested, have natural adult proportions, individual fictional features, a few quiet nearly-flat shaped PAPER pieces and minimal eyes; no low-poly faceting, doll heads or generic racial caricature. Clothing is physically folded fibrous cream paper, with truly cut loose fringe and separate flat dark-paper appliques where requested. Clothing shapes continue the reviewed reconstruction, not modern commercial dress and not claimed a dated universal traditional uniform. Do not copy any living person's portrait or body-paint pattern.
No text, letters, labels, numbers, arrows, logo or watermark. No added people or animals except exactly requested. No invented clan symbols, runes, glow, aura, European fantasy or universal ceremonial costume. No photoreal wood, dirt, water, clay or fabric; no smooth digital painting, photomontage, glossy plastic, resin, sculpted CGI or blurred depth that hides construction. Maintain requested anatomy. No sexualisation, exposed genitalia, gore or explicit violence.

Primary request: Nibagïeño, daughter of Dïïjoma and the boa's caretaker. An IDENTITY SHEET showing the SAME fictional adult woman approximately 25 years old in THREE full-body views: front, side, back. Three heads and six bare feet entirely visible; each body approximately 60 percent image height, reasonably large for face and garment reading. Quiet attentive expression, medium warm-brown paper skin, straight black hair to the shoulders, a longer oval adult face, natural brows and small eyes, no makeup. A loose straight cream fibrous calf-length sleeveless garment with a broad square neck, short irregular cut fringe at the hem, dark brown triangular appliques at the front neck and two broad crossed angular bands across its front. These are the previously reviewed editorial clothing shapes; back has NO decorative motifs, not documented. Keep identical hair, garment, small single strand of understated reddish and pale round paper bead shapes, and a plain fine fibre wrist tie in all three views. The necklace and wrist tie refer only to her dressed presentation state; they are not invented sacred patterns. Arms at rest, no pose of dancing, feeding, seduction or distress. No starch ball, snake, vessel, crown, feathers, facial paint or additional people. Deep but sparse low riverbank forest layers, cream hem strips visibly separated and curled, a small fold down the dress, seams and quiet paper-thickness shadows on hair and face. Natural human features rather than exaggerated polygonal modelling.

Primary request: Ecofaiyaño, the OTHER daughter of Dïïjoma; keep her separate from her sister Nibagïeño. An identity sheet of ONE SAME fictional adult woman about 32 years old, front view, side view and back view, three complete bodies, all heads and bare feet fully in frame. Medium warm-brown paper skin, calm practical expression, a subtly broader face and stronger brow than Nibagïeño, straight black chin-length hair, a slightly sturdier natural adult build. She is equally dignified, not a beauty-versus-ugliness comparison. Loose straight sleeveless cream fibrous dress ending below the knee, wide square neckline, only a short dark-brown row of small triangular appliques at the FRONT neckline, a plain undecorated back and a short irregular cut fringe at the hem. No crossed waist bands, no beads, bracelet, hairband, crown, paint or flowers. The construction resembles the reviewed cream fibre garment, an editorial proposal, not claimed historical costume for this named person. Three views with identical face, proportions, hair and dress. Arms relaxed, hands five fingers, feet natural. Context is sparse paper forest ground outside an ordinary low palm-covered maloca, only a modest fragment of rough post and hanging palm strips at the image edge, not a new architectural hero. Lift the cut hem strips, fold the shoulders and dress down a few quiet planes, give hair and face visible thin layered-paper edges without faceting the face. No flames, her father, snake, tragedy, food preparation or symbolic halo.

Primary request: a BOTANICAL SHEET of the narrative coca plant, using Erythroxylum coca only as a morphological comparison, not identification of a particular Indigenous cultivar. One complete modest woody shrub fills the left and centre, its visible trunk, branches, entire crown and ground junction all in frame, on irregular young chagra earth with a few fallen woody residues and receding forest, not an industrial plantation. Slender branching reddish-brown paper stems; SIMPLE alternating oval to elliptic leaves with entire non-serrated margins, short petioles, clear centre vein. The leaf is not compound and not the radial lobed yuca leaf. On the right a slightly enlarged single branch with several leaves and a separate enlarged individual leaf; supporting details are visibly contextual model studies, not giant leaves growing on another species. Small white five-petalled flower and a few small red oval fruits on the main shrub can remain secondary, not huge tomatoes or pepper pods. Make every leaf an individual broad matte-green cut-paper piece with a fine folded midrib and narrow raised cut-paper veins; upper and lower leaf planes gently twist away from each other with real air and sharply visible cast shadows. Exaggerate cut-paper construction while preserving leaf anatomy. Ground layered torn brown paper, dark woody remnants are folded charcoal paper, full-bleed forest behind. No person, face, baskets, powder, cigarettes, drug imagery, processing steps, recipe or comparison claiming wild and cultivated types can be diagnosed here.

Primary request: a BOTANICAL SHEET of yarumo, a Cecropia-like forest tree used as a morphology comparison without fixing the story's species. A complete young tree, straight relatively pale slender trunk, tiered sparse branches and entire leafy crown visible, with several LARGE SIMPLE deeply palmately-lobed rounded leaves, each a single connected leaf blade with about 7 to 9 broad lobes, not seven independent narrow yuca leaflets. Long petioles attach toward the interior of the palmate blade. Dark matte-green upper leaf faces and noticeably pale cream-grey undersides. At the right, two enlarged leaf studies show upper and lower sides with their folded branching paper midribs, alongside a modest exposed branching root study at ground level, roots NOT bird toes. Every broad lobe cut with visible paper edges, some folds lifting individual lobes and showing the light underside, seams casting long legible paper shadows. Trunk is rolled and folded cream and brown paper, not photographic bark, and root branches are curled layered paper strips. Low dense Amazonian forest understorey with multiple separate paper depth planes continues to all image edges. No magical wings, eagle, human, feathers, glowing roots, star constellation or bowl of ash. The symbolic transformation is documented in the bible but this asset is the plant's own complete body and supporting anatomy.

Primary request: a BOTANICAL SHEET of the tobacco linked to rebirth in the Uuikï story, with Nicotiana tabacum as a visual comparison only, not a taxonomic identification of the traditional plant. One complete upright plant with broad simple alternate ovate-to-elliptic tapering leaves, entire slightly wavy margins, larger low leaves and smaller upper leaves, leaves close to and partly clasping the main stem. An airy branching top bears a small number of long pale pinkish-cream tubular flowers with short five-lobed mouths, not daisies or orange fruits. Entire plant, stem base and all flowers fully in frame. A single enlarged folded leaf and a modest tubular-flower detail at the lower right, naturally nested into contextual paper ground, no separate specimen frame. Thick layered matt-green leaf pieces curl out from the stalk, raised narrow veins made of thinner cut-paper strips, emphatic short cast shadows under every lifted leaf. Dry pale-brown PAPER earth, a few charcoal-grey PAPER remnants in the ground refer quietly to narrative rebirth; no literal body, blood or grave. A mixed-height chagra forest border recedes through strongly spaced cut-paper silhouette layers and continues full bleed. No human figure, smoke, cigarette, packaged tobacco, medicine bottle, manufacturing process, ritual instructions, halo or human face emerging from a flower.

Primary request: an OBJECT IDENTITY SHEET for Uuikï, the speaking heart inherited as a SPHERE, never an anatomical human heart or anthropomorphic Father. Two views in one continuous full-bleed warm, dim-but-readable maloca space. Left: the complete palm-sized dark charcoal-brown matte sphere resting directly in a modest loose pale fibre lining on the earth-paper floor; its construction is a small number of broad curved PAPER gores with visible narrow seams and overlapping edges, like a carefully assembled paper orb, not a crystal, jewel, planet, decorative ball with runes or a wrinkled anatomical organ. Right: the SAME sphere visible halfway inside a close-woven cream and brown oval basket that cradles it softly. The basket's lower walls must be a tightly interleaved continuous weave without open holes, with small irregular raised cut-paper fibre-strip edges and clearly visible diagonal overlaps and cast shadows. A modest rim, no grand lid, no dangling charms. Both sphere and basket shown completely, no crops, roughly comparable scale. A partial rough maloca post and hanging palm paper strips recede far behind, consistent with a low broad palm-covered house, no modern furniture. Ground is layered earth-paper, object shadows broad and clear, deeper forest-paper seen only at a narrow distant doorway. Tangible paper relief is emphatic but the surface is calm. No glowing aura, painted sacred motif, red heart icon, baby, face, hands, deity, fireworks, magical orbit or speech lettering.

Primary request: an OBJECT SHEET of a long adult hunting blowpipe and a smaller episode blowpipe, kept as two separate objects associated with Jitoma and Nokaido. Long narrow STRAIGHT wooden tubes, not arrows, rifles, bamboo flutes, bows or spears. Show the entire long tube diagonally from lower left toward upper right with both ends visible and breathing room; a second substantially shorter tube below it, also complete, both in the same quiet continuous forest-floor context. Dark brown and charcoal tubular bodies made from long rolled and folded PAPER strips, modest pale plant-fibre-paper bindings, a small widened pale wood-like paper mouthpiece at the near end; no gun stock, trigger, chamber, metal blade or feathered staff. One small slender paper dart with a tiny cream vegetable-down tuft near its blunt end appears below, visibly much smaller than a tube; a slightly enlarged mouthpiece detail nearby is only supporting morphology, not construction instructions or an exploded manufacturing diagram. Show crisp narrow inner paper edges along overlapping tube pieces and a believable dark bore opening, binding strands crossing and projecting tiny shadows; all surfaces remain matte cut paper, never photographic wood. Forest paper layers, leaf litter and a gently raised low root fill all edges without a presentation board.
